correctness.rationale: For each ordered spin-exchange pair the two adjoint dissipators send O_i to O_j-O_i and O_j to O_i-O_j, as exact two-qubit operator identities, irrespective of entanglement. The diagonal Ising Hamiltonian commutes with O_i and the anchor operators send O_i to s_i I-O_i. Summing both incoming and outgoing ordered arcs yields c_ij=(1-lambda_i)w_ij+(1-lambda_j)w_ji and the exact symmetric-Laplacian flow. Comparing off-diagonal coefficients with the source's directed FJ flow gives equivalence for every opinion vector exactly when all rates (1-lambda_i)w_ij vanish. The Laplacian quadratic form proves equilibrium and consensus assertions. Exact-rational verification of the 2^n diagonal Markov generator identity passed 48 parameter matrices (n=2,...,5) and separate three-agent unanchored and anchored witnesses. Finite tests supplement, not replace, local operator algebra.

originality.rationale: This is a strictly model-specific comparison of equations (14) and (34) in Chu (2026). The full-text source writes bidirectional two-body spin-exchange jumps but in its FJ reduction omits contributions when the monitored agent is the second member of an ordered arc. Consequently its directed first-moment claim and associated interpretation of numerical discrepancies as feedback of quantum correlations do not follow from the written generator. The exact incoming-arc correction, necessary-and-sufficient no-go, and contrasting exact consensus/anchored equilibria are not stated in the inspected main equations or appendix. Symmetric exclusion moment closure and spin-chain/exclusion correspondences are classical established theory, acknowledged as broader prior coverage. The claim does not pretend novelty of generic graph diffusion. Indexed searches and accessible historical claim comparisons found no specific equivalent analysis, but unindexed correction or erratum remains possible.

value.rationale: The paper's stated directed Friedkin–Johnsen recovery is a foundational model-validation claim. The new comparison rules out that reduction for all genuinely active two-body exchange choices and shows the full Lindblad expected opinions do not depend on interagent correlations, contradicting a causal explanation of full-vs-mean-field discrepancies. Two exact rational three-agent witnesses produce different predicted consensus values or anchored equilibria while obeying every stated parameter restriction. This is a substantive mathematically motivated boundary for modeling directional social influence and for interpreting quantum opinions, not a minor sign convention or parameter renaming.
